_note: Our own wording. The first-session setup the book suggests (Core p.40-41): who the squad is, who gives it orders, and some history between the pilots (the book's own d20 tables stay in the book; these lists are ours, in the same spirit), plus the table's tone, focus and content choices. Tone and focus only change which of our generated stories come up; content toggles take our own themes out of the generators. None of it changes a rule.
identity: A mercenary company with a name still to make
Union regulars, a long way from home
Locals the Union recruited to defend their own world
A planetary guard's best and only lancers
Bounty hunters with very large guns
Corporate security that answers awkward questions
Explorers sent ahead of the colony ships
A crew of former smugglers going straight, mostly
Sworn knights of an old order
Pilgrims who fight for their faith
Test pilots for a company that isn't telling them everything
The last squad of a broken army
Rebels who need the frontier on their side
Volunteers who answered a call for help

patrons.text: Our own code, and nobody else
The mentor who founded the squad
A noble house we're sworn to
The people of the world we protect

squad_history._note: Our own writing. The squad's shared history, made from what the players already chose for their pilots (backgrounds and origins): two pilots from the same world know each other, and so on. Shown as a short summary to edit or reroll; relationships are story flavour (Bonds), no rules effect.
homeworld: {a} and {b} both grew up on {what}. They knew each other's families before they knew each other.
{a} and {b} are both from {what}; they found that out over a bad drink and have been friends since.
{a} and {b} left {what} on the same transport, years apart, and still argue about which way home is.
upbringing: {a} and {b} share a {what} upbringing, and it shows in how they talk.
{a} and {b} were both raised {what}. They recognised it in each other on day one.
employer: {a} and {b} both used to work for {what}, and neither talks about why they left.
{a} and {b} first met on {what}'s payroll. They were on opposite shifts and opposite sides of a complaint.
specialty: {a} and {b} are both {what}s; they compare notes and keep score.
{a} taught {b} half of what makes a good {what}. {b} won't admit it.
background: {a} and {b} share a past as {what}: they trust each other's instincts.
{a} and {b} were both {what} once. They don't always agree what that means.
none: {a} and {b} met the day the squad formed. First impressions were mixed.
{a} pulled {b} out of trouble on their first job together; {b} still owes them one.
{a} and {b} share a bunk room and a running card game.
{b} took {a}'s seat on the transport out. They've been squabbling about it ever since.

history.text: Which of you grew up on the same street as me?
Which of you nearly got me killed, once?
Which of you did I fall for? Is it over?
Which of you have I flown beside for years?
Which of you doesn't trust me yet?
Which of you closes down the bar with me?
Which of you taught me to fly?
Which of you was stranded with me, somewhere awful?
Which of you was there on my first drop?
Which of you comes to me for advice?
Which of you knows the thing I never talk about?
Which of you thinks you've got me figured out?
Which of you have I always tried to outdo?
Which of you do I owe my life to?
Which of you never expected to see me again?
Which of you will stand by me, whatever happens?

hopeful.name: Hopeful
hopeful.text: People can be saved. Fewer twists, more jobs that help people.

heroic.name: Heroic
heroic.text: Big stakes, bold rescues, rivals worth beating.

gritty.name: Gritty
gritty.text: Nobody's clean. More twists, betrayals and hard choices.

mercenary.name: Mercenary
mercenary.text: It's a job. Deals, salvage and who pays best.

combat.name: Combat first
combat.text: Get to the fights. Shorter downtime, less chatter between missions.

story.name: Story first
story.text: Longer downtimes (two actions each, as the book allows for long ones, Core p.50) and more time with the squad.

civilian_harm.name: Civilians in danger
civilian_harm.text: Twists where civilians get caught in the fighting.

nhp_themes.name: NHP minds
nhp_themes.text: Stories about NHPs as thinking, suffering minds.

betrayal.name: Betrayal
betrayal.text: Patrons who lie, leaks, turncoats, the betrayal arc.
